name: Binary to Decimal
expr: Decimal = Σ(digit × 2^position), position starting at 0 from right

name: Decimal to Binary
expr: Repeatedly divide decimal number by 2, read remainders bottom to top

name: Binary to Octal
expr: Group binary digits in 3s from right, convert each group to octal digit

name: Binary to Hexadecimal
expr: Group binary digits in 4s from right, convert each group to hex digit

name: Octal to Decimal
expr: Decimal = Σ(digit × 8^position)

name: Hexadecimal to Decimal
expr: Decimal = Σ(digit × 16^position)

name: 1's Complement
expr: Flip every bit (0→1, 1→0)

name: 2's Complement
expr: 2's Complement = 1's Complement + 1

name: Unsigned Binary Range (n bits)
expr: Range = 0 to 2ⁿ − 1

name: BCD (Binary Coded Decimal)
expr: Each decimal digit represented by its own 4-bit binary code

name: ASCII Value Range
expr: Standard ASCII = 0 to 127 (7-bit)

name: Number of Addressable Bytes (n address lines)
expr: Bytes = 2ⁿ

name: Floating Point Bias (IEEE 754 Single)
expr: Bias = 127, Exponent stored = Actual exponent + 127

name: AND Gate
expr: Y = A · B (Y = 1 only if A = 1 and B = 1)

name: OR Gate
expr: Y = A + B (Y = 1 if A = 1 or B = 1)

name: NOT Gate
expr: Y = A' (inverts input)

name: XOR Gate
expr: Y = A ⊕ B (Y = 1 only when A ≠ B)

name: XNOR Gate
expr: Y = (A ⊕ B)′ (Y = 1 only when A = B)

name: Idempotent Law
expr: A · A = A, A + A = A

name: Absorption Law
expr: A + (A · B) = A, A · (A + B) = A

name: Number of Rows in Truth Table
expr: Rows = 2ⁿ, for n input variables

name: Sum of Products (SOP)
expr: Boolean expression written as OR of AND terms (minterms)

name: Product of Sums (POS)
expr: Boolean expression written as AND of OR terms (maxterms)

name: Karnaugh Map (K-Map) (concept)
expr: graphical method to simplify Boolean expressions by grouping adjacent 1s

name: Half Adder Sum
expr: Sum = A ⊕ B, Carry = A · B

name: Full Adder Sum
expr: Sum = A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin, Cout = AB + Cin(A ⊕ B)

name: Multiplexer Output Lines
expr: A 2ⁿ:1 MUX has n select lines

name: Order of Operator Precedence (concept)
expr: () → unary(!,++,--) → *,/,% → +,- → relational → equality → && → || → =

name: Modulus Operator
expr: a % b = remainder after dividing a by b

name: Increment/Decrement (concept)
expr: x++ uses value then adds 1 (post); ++x adds 1 then uses value (pre)

name: Array Index Range (0-based)
expr: Valid indices = 0 to (Size − 1)

name: Array Memory Address (1-D)
expr: Address(A[i]) = Base + i × Size_of_element

name: Array Memory Address (2-D, Row-Major)
expr: Address(A[i][j]) = Base + (i × Cols + j) × Size_of_element

name: Array Memory Address (2-D, Column-Major)
expr: Address(A[i][j]) = Base + (j × Rows + i) × Size_of_element

name: For Loop Iteration Count
expr: Iterations = ⌈(End − Start)/Step⌉

name: String Length (concept)
expr: number of characters before the null terminator (\0) in a C-string

name: Function Call Stack (concept)
expr: each function call pushes a stack frame; return pops it

name: Recursion Base Case (concept)
expr: the condition that stops recursive calls and prevents infinite recursion

name: Type Casting (concept)
expr: explicit conversion of a value from one data type to another

name: Class vs Object (concept)
expr: a class is a blueprint; an object is an instance created from that class

name: Four Pillars of OOP (concept)
expr: Encapsulation, Abstraction, Inheritance, Polymorphism

name: Constructor (concept)
expr: special member function, same name as class, runs automatically on object creation

name: Function Overloading (concept)
expr: same function name with different parameter lists (compile-time polymorphism)

name: Virtual Function (concept)
expr: enables runtime polymorphism by resolving the call to the derived class method

name: Stack (LIFO) (concept)
expr: Last In, First Out — push/pop only at the top

name: Queue (FIFO) (concept)
expr: First In, First Out — insert at rear, remove from front

name: Stack Overflow Condition
expr: Top = Max_Size − 1 and a push is attempted

name: Stack Underflow Condition
expr: Top = −1 and a pop is attempted

name: Circular Queue Rear (Insert)
expr: Rear = (Rear + 1) mod Size

name: Linked List Node (concept)
expr: a node stores data plus a pointer/reference to the next node

name: Singly vs Doubly Linked List (concept)
expr: singly stores next pointer only; doubly stores next and previous pointers

name: Binary Tree Max Nodes at Level L
expr: Max Nodes = 2^L (root at L = 0)

name: Binary Tree Max Nodes (height h)
expr: Max Nodes = 2^(h+1) − 1

name: Minimum Height of Binary Tree (n nodes)
expr: h_min = ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉ − 1

name: Complete Binary Tree Leaf Nodes
expr: Leaf Nodes ≈ ⌈n/2⌉, for n total nodes

name: Binary Search Tree Property
expr: Left subtree keys < node key < Right subtree keys

name: AVL Tree Balance Factor
expr: BF = Height(Left subtree) − Height(Right subtree), must be in {−1, 0, 1}

name: Tree Traversal Orders (concept)
expr: Inorder (L-Root-R), Preorder (Root-L-R), Postorder (L-R-Root)

name: Graph Edges (Undirected, Complete)
expr: Max Edges = n(n−1)/2

name: Graph Edges (Directed, Complete)
expr: Max Edges = n(n−1)

name: Handshaking Lemma
expr: Σ(degree of all vertices) = 2 × Number of Edges

name: Adjacency Matrix Space
expr: Space = O(n²), for n vertices

name: Hash Table Load Factor
expr: α = Number of entries/Number of buckets

name: Hash Function (Division Method)
expr: h(k) = k mod m

name: Linear Probing (Collision Resolution)
expr: h(k, i) = (h(k) + i) mod m

name: Heap Parent Index (0-based array)
expr: Parent(i) = ⌊(i−1)/2⌋

name: Heap Left Child Index
expr: Left(i) = 2i + 1

name: Heap Right Child Index
expr: Right(i) = 2i + 2

name: Min-Heap / Max-Heap Property (concept)
expr: in a min-heap every parent ≤ its children; in a max-heap every parent ≥ its children

name: Big-O Notation (concept)
expr: O(g(n)) describes the worst-case upper bound of an algorithm's growth rate

name: Logarithmic Time
expr: O(log n)

name: Linear Time
expr: O(n)

name: Linearithmic Time
expr: O(n log n)

name: Quadratic Time
expr: O(n²)

name: Exponential Time
expr: O(2ⁿ)

name: Linear Search Complexity
expr: Best = O(1), Worst/Average = O(n)

name: Binary Search Complexity
expr: O(log n), array must be sorted

name: Bubble Sort Complexity
expr: Best = O(n), Worst/Average = O(n²)

name: Selection Sort Complexity
expr: O(n²) in all cases

name: Insertion Sort Complexity
expr: Best = O(n), Worst/Average = O(n²)

name: Merge Sort Complexity
expr: O(n log n) in all cases

name: Quick Sort Complexity
expr: Best/Average = O(n log n), Worst = O(n²)

name: Heap Sort Complexity
expr: O(n log n) in all cases

name: Master Theorem (Divide & Conquer)
expr: T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n), compares f(n) to n^(log_b a)

name: Space Complexity (concept)
expr: the amount of extra memory an algorithm uses relative to input size

name: Amortized Analysis (concept)
expr: average cost per operation over a worst-case sequence of operations

name: Dynamic Programming (concept)
expr: breaks a problem into overlapping subproblems and stores results to avoid recomputation

name: Greedy Algorithm (concept)
expr: makes the locally optimal choice at each step, hoping for a global optimum

name: Dijkstra's Algorithm (concept)
expr: finds shortest paths from a source vertex in a weighted graph with non-negative edges

name: P vs NP (concept)
expr: P = problems solvable in polynomial time; NP = problems verifiable in polynomial time

name: Primary Key (concept)
expr: a column (or set of columns) that uniquely identifies each row in a table

name: Foreign Key (concept)
expr: a column that references the primary key of another table, linking the two

name: Relational Algebra — Selection
expr: σ(condition)(Table) — filters rows meeting a condition

name: Relational Algebra — Projection
expr: π(columns)(Table) — selects specific columns

name: Relational Algebra — Join
expr: R ⋈ S — combines rows from two tables on a related column

name: 1NF (First Normal Form) (concept)
expr: all columns hold atomic (indivisible) values, no repeating groups

name: 2NF (Second Normal Form) (concept)
expr: 1NF plus no partial dependency of any column on part of a composite key

name: 3NF (Third Normal Form) (concept)
expr: 2NF plus no transitive dependency of non-key columns on other non-key columns

name: BCNF (Boyce-Codd Normal Form) (concept)
expr: every determinant in a functional dependency must be a candidate key

name: ACID Properties (concept)
expr: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — guarantee reliable transactions

name: Functional Dependency Notation
expr: X → Y means X uniquely determines Y

name: Entity-Relationship (ER) Cardinality (concept)
expr: describes 1:1, 1:N, or M:N relationships between entities

name: SQL Query Execution Order (concept)
expr: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY

name: B-Tree Index (concept)
expr: a balanced tree structure used by databases to speed up row lookups

name: OSI Model Layers (concept)
expr: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application

name: TCP/IP Model Layers (concept)
expr: Network Access, Internet, Transport, Application

name: IPv4 Address Format
expr: 32 bits, written as 4 octets, e.g. 192.168.1.1

name: IPv6 Address Format
expr: 128 bits, written as 8 groups of hexadecimal, e.g. 2001:0db8::1

name: Number of Hosts per Subnet
expr: Usable Hosts = 2^(32−prefix) − 2

name: Number of Subnets
expr: Subnets = 2^(borrowed bits)

name: Bandwidth vs Throughput (concept)
expr: bandwidth = maximum theoretical data rate; throughput = actual achieved data rate

name: Data Transfer Time
expr: Time = File Size/Bandwidth

name: Propagation Delay
expr: Propagation Delay = Distance/Propagation Speed

name: Transmission Delay
expr: Transmission Delay = Packet Size/Bandwidth

name: Total Latency (Simple)
expr: Latency = Transmission Delay + Propagation Delay + Queuing Delay + Processing Delay

name: Nyquist Bit Rate (Noiseless Channel)
expr: BitRate = 2 × Bandwidth × log₂(L), L = signal levels

name: Shannon Capacity (Noisy Channel)
expr: Capacity = Bandwidth × log₂(1 + SNR)

name: CRC / Checksum (concept)
expr: error-detection codes that verify data integrity after transmission

name: Three-Way TCP Handshake (concept)
expr: SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK, used to establish a reliable TCP connection

name: TCP vs UDP (concept)
expr: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable; UDP is connectionless and faster but unreliable

name: DNS Resolution (concept)
expr: translates a human-readable domain name into its numeric IP address

name: CPU Utilization
expr: CPU Utilization = (Busy Time/Total Time) × 100

name: Throughput (OS)
expr: Throughput = Number of Processes Completed/Total Time

name: Turnaround Time
expr: Turnaround Time = Completion Time − Arrival Time

name: Waiting Time
expr: Waiting Time = Turnaround Time − Burst Time

name: Response Time
expr: Response Time = Time of first CPU response − Arrival Time

name: FCFS Scheduling (concept)
expr: First Come, First Served — processes executed strictly in arrival order

name: SJF Scheduling (concept)
expr: Shortest Job First — process with smallest burst time runs next

name: Round Robin Scheduling (concept)
expr: each process gets a fixed time quantum in cyclic order

name: Page Fault (concept)
expr: occurs when a requested page is not present in main memory

name: Page Fault Rate
expr: Page Fault Rate = Number of Page Faults/Total Page References

name: Effective Access Time (with paging)
expr: EAT = (1−p) × Memory Access Time + p × Page Fault Time, p = fault rate

name: Number of Pages
expr: Pages = ⌈Process Size/Page Size⌉

name: Number of Frames
expr: Frames = Physical Memory Size/Page Size

name: Logical Address (Paging)
expr: Logical Address = (Page Number, Offset)

name: Deadlock Necessary Conditions (concept)
expr: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait

name: Semaphore (concept)
expr: an integer variable used with wait()/signal() to control access to shared resources

name: Belady's Anomaly (concept)
expr: page fault rate can increase even when more frames are allocated (in FIFO)

name: CPU Clock Cycle Time
expr: Cycle Time = 1/Clock Frequency

name: CPU Execution Time
expr: Execution Time = Instruction Count × CPI × Cycle Time

name: MIPS (Million Instructions per Second)
expr: MIPS = Instruction Count/(Execution Time × 10⁶)

name: Speedup (Amdahl's Law)
expr: Speedup = 1/((1 − f) + f/S), f = fraction improved, S = speedup of that fraction

name: Cache Hit Ratio
expr: Hit Ratio = Number of Hits/Total Memory Accesses

name: Average Memory Access Time (AMAT)
expr: AMAT = Hit Time + Miss Rate × Miss Penalty

name: Pipeline Speedup (Ideal)
expr: Speedup = Number of Pipeline Stages (ideal, no stalls)

name: Pipeline Execution Time
expr: Time = (k + n − 1) × Clock Cycle, k = stages, n = instructions

name: Memory Address Space
expr: Address Space = 2^(number of address bits)

name: Moore's Law (concept)
expr: the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years

name: RISC vs CISC (concept)
expr: RISC uses simple, fixed-length instructions; CISC uses complex, variable-length instructions

name: Software Development Life Cycle (concept)
expr: Requirements → Design → Implementation → Testing → Deployment → Maintenance

name: Lines of Code (LOC) Metric (concept)
expr: a simple size measure counting the number of code lines in a program

name: COCOMO Effort Estimate (Basic)
expr: Effort = a × (KLOC)^b person-months

name: Function Point Analysis (concept)
expr: estimates software size based on functionality delivered to the user

name: Defect Density
expr: Defect Density = Number of Defects/Size (KLOC or Function Points)

name: Test Coverage
expr: Coverage = (Lines/Branches Tested/Total Lines/Branches) × 100

name: Cyclomatic Complexity
expr: V(G) = E − N + 2, E = edges, N = nodes in control flow graph

name: Software Reliability (concept)
expr: the probability that software performs without failure for a given time period

name: Agile Velocity
expr: Velocity = Story Points Completed/Sprint

name: SOLID Principles (concept)
expr: Single Responsibility, Open-Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion

name: Caesar Cipher Encryption
expr: Cipher = (Plain + Shift) mod 26

name: Caesar Cipher Decryption
expr: Plain = (Cipher − Shift) mod 26

name: Symmetric vs Asymmetric Encryption (concept)
expr: symmetric uses one shared key; asymmetric uses a public/private key pair

name: RSA Key Generation (concept)
expr: choose primes p, q → n = p×q, compute φ(n) = (p−1)(q−1), pick e, d such that e·d ≡ 1 mod φ(n)

name: RSA Encryption
expr: C = M^e mod n

name: RSA Decryption
expr: M = C^d mod n

name: Hashing (concept)
expr: one-way function that maps data of any size to a fixed-size digest, used for integrity checks

name: Digital Signature (concept)
expr: a hash of the message encrypted with the sender's private key, verified with their public key

name: Brute Force Key Space
expr: Possible Keys = 2^(key length in bits)

name: CIA Triad (concept)
expr: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability — the three core goals of information security

name: Finite Automaton (concept)
expr: a machine with a finite set of states used to recognize regular languages

name: DFA vs NFA (concept)
expr: DFA has exactly one transition per input per state; NFA may have zero, one, or many

name: Regular Expression (concept)
expr: a pattern describing a set of strings accepted by a finite automaton

name: Context-Free Grammar (concept)
expr: a set of production rules of the form A → α used to generate context-free languages

name: Turing Machine (concept)
expr: an abstract machine with an infinite tape that models general computation

name: Decidability (concept)
expr: a problem is decidable if an algorithm exists that always halts with a correct yes/no answer

name: Chomsky Hierarchy (concept)
expr: Type 0 (Recursively Enumerable) ⊃ Type 1 (Context-Sensitive) ⊃ Type 2 (Context-Free) ⊃ Type 3 (Regular)

name: Accuracy
expr: Accuracy = (TP + TN)/(TP + TN + FP + FN)

name: Precision
expr: Precision = TP/(TP + FP)

name: Recall (Sensitivity)
expr: Recall = TP/(TP + FN)

name: F1 Score
expr: F1 = 2 × (Precision × Recall)/(Precision + Recall)

name: Mean Squared Error (Loss)
expr: MSE = (1/n) × Σ(yᵢ − ŷᵢ)²

name: ReLU Activation Function
expr: ReLU(x) = max(0, x)

name: Gradient Descent Update Rule
expr: θ = θ − α × ∇J(θ), α = learning rate

name: Euclidean Distance (k-NN)
expr: d(p,q) = √Σ(pᵢ − qᵢ)²

name: Bayes' Theorem (Naive Bayes)
expr: P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B)

name: Overfitting vs Underfitting (concept)
expr: overfitting learns noise in training data; underfitting fails to capture the underlying pattern

name: Train/Test Split (concept)
expr: dataset is divided into a training set (to fit the model) and a test set (to evaluate it)

name: SR Flip-Flop (concept)
expr: basic latch with Set and Reset inputs; invalid state when S=R=1

name: D Flip-Flop (concept)
expr: output Q follows input D on each clock edge, avoids the invalid SR state

name: JK Flip-Flop Toggle
expr: when J = K = 1, output toggles on each clock pulse

name: T Flip-Flop (concept)
expr: output toggles every clock pulse when T = 1, holds when T = 0

name: Modulus of a Counter
expr: MOD-N counter cycles through N states before repeating

name: Flip-Flops Needed for MOD-N Counter
expr: n = ⌈log₂ N⌉

name: Shift Register (concept)
expr: a chain of flip-flops that shifts stored bits left or right on each clock pulse

name: Register Capacity
expr: an n-bit register can store 2ⁿ distinct values

name: Propagation Delay of a Gate (concept)
expr: the time taken for a gate's output to change after its input changes

name: Gray Code Property (concept)
expr: only one bit changes between two successive values

name: Binary to Gray Code
expr: G₀ = B₀, Gᵢ = Bᵢ ⊕ Bᵢ₋₁

name: Excess-3 Code
expr: Excess-3 = BCD code + 0011 (adds 3 to each decimal digit before converting)

name: Parity Bit (Even Parity)
expr: added bit makes the total number of 1s in the word even

name: Parity Bit (Odd Parity)
expr: added bit makes the total number of 1s in the word odd

name: Number of Subsets of a Set
expr: Subsets = 2ⁿ, for a set with n elements

name: Number of Proper Subsets
expr: Proper Subsets = 2ⁿ − 1

name: Permutations (nPr)
expr: nPr = n!/(n − r)!

name: Combinations (nCr)
expr: nCr = n!/(r!(n − r)!)

name: Logical Implication Truth Table (concept)
expr: p → q is false only when p is true and q is false

name: Biconditional (p ↔ q) (concept)
expr: true only when p and q have the same truth value

name: Contrapositive (concept)
expr: the contrapositive of p → q is ¬q → ¬p, and is logically equivalent to it

name: Relation Reflexive Property (concept)
expr: every element is related to itself: (a,a) ∈ R for all a

name: Relation Symmetric Property (concept)
expr: if (a,b) ∈ R then (b,a) ∈ R

name: Relation Transitive Property (concept)
expr: if (a,b) ∈ R and (b,c) ∈ R then (a,c) ∈ R

name: Equivalence Relation (concept)
expr: a relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive

name: Mathematical Induction (concept)
expr: prove base case P(1), then prove P(k) ⟹ P(k+1) to conclude P(n) for all n

name: Pigeonhole Principle (concept)
expr: if n items are placed into m containers and n > m, at least one container holds more than one item

name: Graph Coloring — Chromatic Number (concept)
expr: the minimum number of colors needed so no two adjacent vertices share a color

name: Euler's Formula for Planar Graphs
expr: V − E + F = 2, V = vertices, E = edges, F = faces

name: Compiler vs Interpreter (concept)
expr: a compiler translates the whole program to machine code before running; an interpreter executes line by line

name: Phases of a Compiler (concept)
expr: Lexical Analysis → Syntax Analysis → Semantic Analysis → Intermediate Code → Optimization → Code Generation

name: Lexical Analysis (concept)
expr: breaks source code into tokens (keywords, identifiers, operators, etc.)

name: Syntax Analysis / Parsing (concept)
expr: checks token sequence against grammar rules and builds a parse tree

name: Top-Down vs Bottom-Up Parsing (concept)
expr: top-down builds the parse tree from root to leaves; bottom-up builds it from leaves to root

name: Symbol Table (concept)
expr: a data structure storing information about identifiers used in a program

name: Static vs Dynamic Typing (concept)
expr: static typing checks types at compile time; dynamic typing checks types at runtime

name: Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference (concept)
expr: pass by value copies the argument; pass by reference passes the original variable's address

name: Garbage Collection (concept)
expr: automatic reclaiming of memory occupied by objects no longer referenced by the program

name: Exception Handling (concept)
expr: try/catch blocks used to detect and handle runtime errors gracefully

name: HTTP Status Codes (concept)
expr: 2xx Success, 3xx Redirection, 4xx Client Error, 5xx Server Error

name: HTTP GET vs POST (concept)
expr: GET requests data and appends parameters to the URL; POST sends data in the request body

name: Client-Server Model (concept)
expr: clients send requests to a server, which processes them and returns responses

name: Frontend vs Backend (concept)
expr: frontend handles what the user sees (HTML/CSS/JS); backend handles server logic, data, and APIs

name: Cookies vs Sessions (concept)
expr: cookies are stored on the client; sessions are stored on the server and referenced by a session ID

name: REST API (concept)
expr: an architectural style using HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) to access and manipulate resources

name: DOM (Document Object Model) (concept)
expr: a tree-structured representation of an HTML page that JavaScript can read and modify

name: Responsive Web Design (concept)
expr: layouts that adapt to different screen sizes using flexible grids and media queries

name: Git Repository (concept)
expr: a folder tracked by Git that stores the full history of changes to its files

name: Git Commit (concept)
expr: a saved snapshot of changes in the repository at a point in time

name: Git Branch (concept)
expr: an independent line of development that can be merged back into the main codebase

name: Merge Conflict (concept)
expr: occurs when two branches change the same lines of a file differently and Git cannot auto-merge

name: Push vs Pull (concept)
expr: push uploads local commits to a remote repository; pull downloads and merges remote changes locally

name: IaaS / PaaS / SaaS (concept)
expr: Infrastructure, Platform, and Software as a Service — increasing levels of managed cloud abstraction

name: Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling (concept)
expr: horizontal scaling adds more machines; vertical scaling adds more power to an existing machine

name: Load Balancing (concept)
expr: distributes incoming requests across multiple servers to optimize resource use and avoid overload

name: CAP Theorem
expr: a distributed system can guarantee at most 2 of: Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance

name: Latency vs Throughput (Distributed Systems) (concept)
expr: latency = time for one request to complete; throughput = requests handled per unit time

name: Virtualization (concept)
expr: running multiple virtual machines on one physical machine via a hypervisor

name: Containerization (concept)
expr: packaging an application with its dependencies into a lightweight, portable container (e.g. Docker)

name: File Allocation Methods (concept)
expr: Contiguous, Linked, and Indexed allocation are the three main disk space allocation methods

name: FCFS Disk Scheduling (concept)
expr: requests served strictly in the order they arrive

name: SSTF Disk Scheduling (concept)
expr: Shortest Seek Time First — services the request closest to the current head position

name: SCAN Disk Scheduling (concept)
expr: the disk arm moves in one direction servicing requests, reverses at the end (elevator algorithm)

name: Disk Seek Time
expr: Total Access Time = Seek Time + Rotational Latency + Transfer Time

name: RAID 0 (concept)
expr: striping data across multiple disks for speed, with no redundancy

name: RAID 1 (concept)
expr: mirroring — data is duplicated identically across two disks for redundancy

name: Pixel Resolution
expr: Resolution = Horizontal Pixels × Vertical Pixels

name: Image File Size (Uncompressed)
expr: Size (bits) = Width × Height × Bits per Pixel

name: Aspect Ratio
expr: Aspect Ratio = Width : Height

name: RGB Color Model (concept)
expr: colors formed by combining Red, Green, and Blue light values, each typically 0–255

name: Frame Rate
expr: FPS = Number of Frames/Time in seconds

name: 2D Translation Transformation
expr: x' = x + tx, y' = y + ty

name: 2D Scaling Transformation
expr: x' = x × sx, y' = y × sy

name: Confusion Matrix (concept)
expr: a table showing True Positives, True Negatives, False Positives, and False Negatives

name: Entropy (Information Theory)
expr: H(X) = −Σ p(x) log₂ p(x)

name: Information Gain (Decision Trees)
expr: IG = Entropy(Parent) − Weighted Average Entropy(Children)

name: K-Means Clustering Objective
expr: minimizes Σ ||xᵢ − centroid_of_cluster||²

name: Normalization (Min-Max Scaling)
expr: x' = (x − min)/(max − min)

name: Standardization (Z-score)
expr: x' = (x − μ)/σ

name: Singleton Pattern (concept)
expr: ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it

name: Factory Pattern (concept)
expr: creates objects without specifying the exact class of object to be created

name: Observer Pattern (concept)
expr: defines a one-to-many dependency so that when one object changes state, all dependents are notified

name: MVC Architecture (concept)
expr: Model (data), View (UI), Controller (logic) — separates concerns in an application

name: Decimal to BCD
expr: convert each decimal digit separately into its 4-bit binary equivalent

name: Hexadecimal Addition (concept)
expr: add digit by digit in base 16, carrying 1 whenever a column sum reaches 16

name: Fixed-Point vs Floating-Point (concept)
expr: fixed-point has a set number of digits after the decimal; floating-point uses a mantissa and exponent for a wider range

name: Overflow in Signed Addition (concept)
expr: occurs when adding two numbers of the same sign produces a result of the opposite sign

name: Application Layer Protocols (concept)
expr: HTTP (web), FTP (files), SMTP (email), DNS (naming), DHCP (IP assignment)

name: Port Number Range
expr: Well-known ports = 0–1023, Registered = 1024–49151, Dynamic/Private = 49152–65535

name: MAC Address Format
expr: 48-bit address written as 6 pairs of hexadecimal digits, e.g. 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E

name: Firewall (concept)
expr: a system that monitors and filters incoming/outgoing network traffic based on security rules

name: VPN (concept)
expr: creates an encrypted tunnel over a public network to securely connect to a private network

name: Backtracking (concept)
expr: explores all possible solutions incrementally and abandons a path as soon as it fails a constraint

name: Bellman-Ford Algorithm (concept)
expr: finds shortest paths from a source vertex, and can handle negative edge weights

name: Kruskal's Algorithm (concept)
expr: builds a minimum spanning tree by adding the smallest edge that doesn't form a cycle

name: Prim's Algorithm (concept)
expr: builds a minimum spanning tree by growing it one vertex at a time from a starting node

name: Breadth-First Search (BFS) Complexity
expr: O(V + E), V = vertices, E = edges

name: Depth-First Search (DFS) Complexity
expr: O(V + E), V = vertices, E = edges

name: Instruction Cycle (concept)
expr: Fetch → Decode → Execute → Store, repeated for every CPU instruction

name: Instruction Format (concept)
expr: an instruction is made up of an Opcode (operation) and Operand(s) (data/address)

name: Addressing Modes (concept)
expr: Immediate, Direct, Indirect, and Register addressing describe how an operand's location is specified

name: Program Counter (PC) (concept)
expr: register holding the memory address of the next instruction to be executed

name: Instruction Register (IR) (concept)
expr: register that holds the instruction currently being decoded or executed

name: Accumulator (concept)
expr: a CPU register that temporarily holds intermediate arithmetic/logic results

name: Machine Cycle Time
expr: Machine Cycle Time = Number of Clock Periods × Clock Period

name: Opcode Bits Needed
expr: Opcode bits = ⌈log₂(number of distinct instructions)⌉

name: Stack-Based vs Register-Based Machines (concept)
expr: stack machines operate on a push/pop stack; register machines operate directly on named registers

name: Interrupt (concept)
expr: a signal that pauses the current program so the CPU can handle a higher-priority event

name: Virtual Memory (concept)
expr: lets a program use more memory than physically available by mapping to disk storage

name: Segmentation (concept)
expr: divides a program into variable-sized logical units (code, data, stack) instead of fixed pages

name: Internal Fragmentation (concept)
expr: wasted space inside an allocated fixed-size block that is larger than what is actually needed

name: External Fragmentation (concept)
expr: free memory becomes scattered in small blocks too small to satisfy new requests

name: FIFO Page Replacement (concept)
expr: replaces the page that has been in memory the longest

name: LRU Page Replacement (concept)
expr: Least Recently Used — replaces the page that hasn't been used for the longest time

name: Optimal Page Replacement (concept)
expr: replaces the page that won't be used for the longest time in the future (theoretical best)

name: Thrashing (concept)
expr: excessive paging activity that causes CPU utilization to drop drastically

name: Segment Table Entry (concept)
expr: stores a segment's base address and its length/limit

name: Working Set (concept)
expr: the set of pages a process actively references in a given time window

name: Hamming Code — Redundant Bits
expr: 2^r ≥ m + r + 1, m = data bits, r = redundant bits

name: Hamming Distance
expr: number of bit positions in which two binary strings of equal length differ

name: Distance Vector Routing (concept)
expr: each router shares its routing table with directly connected neighbors periodically

name: Link State Routing (concept)
expr: each router builds a complete map of the network topology and computes shortest paths independently

name: Stop-and-Wait Protocol (concept)
expr: sender transmits one frame and waits for an acknowledgment before sending the next

name: Sliding Window Protocol (concept)
expr: allows multiple frames to be sent before requiring an acknowledgment, improving throughput

name: Sliding Window Size Formula
expr: Efficiency = W/(1 + 2a), W = window size, a = propagation delay/transmission time

name: Bit Stuffing (concept)
expr: inserts an extra bit into a data stream to prevent it from being confused with a control sequence

name: NAT (Network Address Translation) (concept)
expr: maps private IP addresses inside a network to a single public IP address for internet access

name: Wireless vs Wired Networks (concept)
expr: wireless uses radio signals (no physical medium); wired uses cables for typically faster, more stable links

name: Transaction (concept)
expr: a sequence of database operations treated as a single logical unit of work

name: Concurrency Control (concept)
expr: techniques that ensure correct results when multiple transactions execute simultaneously

name: Deadlock in Databases (concept)
expr: occurs when two or more transactions wait indefinitely for locks held by each other

name: Two-Phase Locking (concept)
expr: a transaction acquires all locks it needs (growing phase) before releasing any (shrinking phase)

name: Dirty Read (concept)
expr: a transaction reads data that another uncommitted transaction has modified

name: Isolation Levels (concept)
expr: Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable — increasing strictness of transaction isolation

name: Indexing (concept)
expr: a data structure that speeds up data retrieval at the cost of extra storage and update overhead

name: Clustered vs Non-Clustered Index (concept)
expr: clustered index sorts and stores data rows in index order; non-clustered index stores a separate pointer structure

name: View (Database) (concept)
expr: a virtual table defined by a stored query, computed dynamically from underlying tables

name: Trigger (concept)
expr: a stored procedure that automatically runs in response to a specified database event

name: Perceptron Output
expr: y = f(Σwᵢxᵢ + b), f = activation function

name: Tanh Activation Function
expr: tanh(x) = (eˣ − e⁻ˣ)/(eˣ + e⁻ˣ)

name: Softmax Function
expr: softmax(zᵢ) = e^zᵢ/Σⱼe^zⱼ

name: Forward Propagation (concept)
expr: input data passes through the network layer by layer to produce an output prediction

name: Backpropagation (concept)
expr: computes gradients of the loss with respect to weights by propagating error backward through the network

name: Cross-Entropy Loss
expr: L = −Σ yᵢ log(ŷᵢ)

name: Learning Rate (concept)
expr: a hyperparameter controlling how large a step gradient descent takes toward the minimum

name: Epoch (concept)
expr: one complete pass of the entire training dataset through the neural network

name: Batch Size (concept)
expr: the number of training samples processed before the model's weights are updated

name: Convolutional Layer (concept)
expr: applies a sliding filter/kernel across the input to detect spatial features like edges

name: Pooling Layer (concept)
expr: reduces the spatial size of feature maps, commonly using max or average pooling

name: Dropout (concept)
expr: randomly disables a fraction of neurons during training to reduce overfitting

name: GCD — Euclidean Algorithm
expr: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b), until b = 0

name: LCM from GCD
expr: lcm(a, b) = (a × b)/gcd(a, b)

name: Modular Addition
expr: (a + b) mod n = ((a mod n) + (b mod n)) mod n

name: Modular Multiplication
expr: (a × b) mod n = ((a mod n) × (b mod n)) mod n

name: Modular Exponentiation
expr: a^b mod n, computed efficiently via repeated squaring

name: Prime Number (concept)
expr: a natural number greater than 1 with no positive divisors other than 1 and itself

name: Sieve of Eratosthenes (concept)
expr: an algorithm to find all primes up to n by iteratively marking multiples of each prime

name: Fermat's Little Theorem
expr: if p is prime, then a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p), for a not divisible by p

name: Euler's Totient Function
expr: φ(n) = number of integers from 1 to n that are coprime to n

name: Coprime Numbers (concept)
expr: two numbers are coprime if their greatest common divisor is 1

name: Huffman Coding (concept)
expr: assigns shorter binary codes to more frequent symbols to minimize total encoded length

name: Lossless vs Lossy Compression (concept)
expr: lossless compression allows exact original data recovery; lossy compression discards some data permanently

name: Compression Ratio
expr: Compression Ratio = Original Size/Compressed Size

name: Run-Length Encoding (RLE) (concept)
expr: replaces sequences of repeated values with a single value and a count

name: Base64 Encoding (concept)
expr: encodes binary data into ASCII text using 64 printable characters, for safe transmission

name: Unicode vs ASCII (concept)
expr: ASCII encodes 128 characters in 7 bits; Unicode supports virtually all world scripts using variable-width encoding

name: UTF-8 Encoding (concept)
expr: a variable-length Unicode encoding using 1 to 4 bytes per character, backward-compatible with ASCII

name: Entropy Coding (concept)
expr: compression technique that encodes symbols based on their probability of occurrence

name: Process vs Thread (concept)
expr: a process has its own memory space; threads within a process share the same memory space

name: Race Condition (concept)
expr: occurs when multiple threads access shared data simultaneously and the outcome depends on timing

name: Mutex (concept)
expr: a locking mechanism ensuring only one thread can access a critical section at a time

name: Critical Section (concept)
expr: a code segment where a process accesses shared resources that must not be executed by more than one process at once

name: Amdahl's Law (Parallel Speedup)
expr: Speedup(N) = 1/((1 − P) + P/N), P = parallel portion, N = number of processors

name: Parallel Efficiency
expr: Efficiency = Speedup/Number of Processors

name: Multithreading (concept)
expr: running multiple threads concurrently within a single process to improve responsiveness or performance

name: Producer-Consumer Problem (concept)
expr: classic synchronization problem where producers generate data and consumers process it via a shared buffer

name: Dining Philosophers Problem (concept)
expr: classic problem illustrating deadlock and resource allocation issues in concurrent systems

name: MapReduce (concept)
expr: a programming model that processes large datasets by splitting work into parallel Map and Reduce phases

name: Embedded System (concept)
expr: a combination of hardware and software designed to perform a specific dedicated function

name: Microcontroller vs Microprocessor (concept)
expr: a microcontroller integrates CPU, memory, and I/O on one chip; a microprocessor needs external memory/I/O chips

name: Real-Time Operating System (RTOS) (concept)
expr: an OS designed to process data and respond within a guaranteed, strict time constraint

name: Native vs Cross-Platform Apps (concept)
expr: native apps are built for one OS using its own SDK; cross-platform apps share one codebase across OSes

name: Battery Life Estimate
expr: Battery Life (hours) = Battery Capacity (mAh)/Average Current Draw (mA)

name: IoT (Internet of Things) (concept)
expr: a network of physical devices embedded with sensors that collect and exchange data over the internet

name: Sensor vs Actuator (concept)
expr: a sensor detects/measures a physical property; an actuator produces physical motion or action in response

name: Sampling Rate (Sensors)
expr: Sampling Rate (Hz) = Number of Samples/Time (seconds)

name: Blockchain (concept)
expr: a distributed, tamper-resistant ledger where each block cryptographically references the previous one

name: Block Hash Linking (concept)
expr: each block stores the hash of the previous block, so altering any block breaks the chain's integrity

name: Proof of Work (concept)
expr: a consensus mechanism requiring nodes to solve a computational puzzle before adding a new block

name: Smart Contract (concept)
expr: self-executing code on a blockchain that automatically enforces the terms of an agreement

name: Quantum Bit (Qubit) (concept)
expr: the basic unit of quantum information that can exist in a superposition of 0 and 1 simultaneously

name: Superposition (concept)
expr: a quantum system's ability to exist in multiple states at once until it is measured

name: Quantum Entanglement (concept)
expr: a phenomenon where the state of one particle is directly correlated with another, regardless of distance

name: Augmented Reality (AR) (concept)
expr: overlays digital content onto the real-world view, typically through a camera or headset

name: Virtual Reality (VR) (concept)
expr: creates a fully immersive, simulated digital environment that replaces the user's real-world view

name: Edge Computing (concept)
expr: processes data closer to where it is generated instead of sending it all to a centralized cloud server

name: Unit Testing (concept)
expr: tests individual components or functions of a program in isolation

name: Integration Testing (concept)
expr: tests how multiple modules work together after being combined

name: Black-Box Testing (concept)
expr: tests functionality without knowledge of the internal code structure

name: White-Box Testing (concept)
expr: tests internal code logic and structure with full knowledge of the implementation

name: Regression Testing (concept)
expr: re-running tests after changes to ensure existing functionality still works correctly

name: Test Case (concept)
expr: a set of conditions and inputs used to verify a specific feature or requirement

name: Boundary Value Analysis (concept)
expr: testing technique focusing on values at the edges of valid input ranges, where errors are most likely

name: Bug Severity vs Priority (concept)
expr: severity measures a bug's impact on the system; priority measures how urgently it should be fixed

name: Usability (concept)
expr: the ease with which users can learn and use a system to achieve their goals effectively

name: Fitts's Law
expr: T = a + b log₂(D/W + 1), T = time to reach target, D = distance, W = target width

name: User-Centered Design (concept)
expr: a design process that focuses on user needs and feedback at every development stage

name: Accessibility (concept)
expr: designing systems usable by people with a wide range of abilities and disabilities

name: Wireframe (concept)
expr: a simplified visual layout showing the structure and placement of elements on a screen before design

name: A/B Testing (concept)
expr: compares two versions of a design with real users to determine which performs better

name: Regex — Any Character
expr: . matches any single character except a newline

name: Regex — Zero or More
expr: * matches zero or more occurrences of the preceding element

name: Regex — One or More
expr: + matches one or more occurrences of the preceding element

name: Regex — Zero or One
expr: ? matches zero or one occurrence of the preceding element

name: Regex — Character Class
expr: [abc] matches any single character among a, b, or c

name: Regex — Anchors
expr: ^ matches the start of a string, $ matches the end of a string

name: Regex — Quantifier Range
expr: {n,m} matches between n and m occurrences of the preceding element

name: String Matching — Naive Approach Complexity
expr: O(n×m), n = text length, m = pattern length

name: Interpolation Search Complexity
expr: Average = O(log log n), Worst = O(n), for uniformly distributed sorted data

name: Jump Search Complexity
expr: O(√n), optimal jump size = √n

name: Counting Sort Complexity
expr: O(n + k), k = range of input values

name: Radix Sort Complexity
expr: O(d × (n + k)), d = number of digits, k = base/range

name: Bucket Sort Complexity
expr: Average = O(n + k), Worst = O(n²)

name: Shell Sort Complexity
expr: depends on gap sequence, typically between O(n log n) and O(n²)

name: Stable vs Unstable Sort (concept)
expr: a stable sort preserves the relative order of equal elements; an unstable sort does not guarantee this

name: In-Place vs Out-of-Place Sort (concept)
expr: in-place sorting uses O(1) extra memory; out-of-place sorting requires additional memory proportional to input size

name: Divide and Conquer (concept)
expr: breaks a problem into smaller subproblems, solves them independently, then combines their results

name: Best, Average, Worst Case (concept)
expr: describe an algorithm's performance under the most favorable, typical, and least favorable input conditions

name: Pushdown Automaton (PDA) (concept)
expr: a finite automaton extended with a stack, used to recognize context-free languages

name: Pumping Lemma (Regular Languages) (concept)
expr: used to prove a language is not regular by showing it cannot be "pumped" while staying in the language

name: Language (Formal Definition) (concept)
expr: a set of strings formed from symbols of a given alphabet

name: Kleene Star (concept)
expr: A* denotes zero or more concatenations of strings from language A

name: NFA to DFA Conversion (concept)
expr: subset construction — each DFA state represents a set of possible NFA states

name: Minimal DFA (concept)
expr: the DFA with the fewest possible states that still accepts exactly the same language

name: Halting Problem (concept)
expr: proven undecidable — no general algorithm can determine whether every program halts on every input

name: NP-Complete Problem (concept)
expr: a problem in NP to which every other NP problem can be reduced in polynomial time

name: Green Computing (concept)
expr: designing and using computers and IT resources in an energy-efficient, environmentally responsible way

name: Open Source vs Proprietary Software (concept)
expr: open source allows free access and modification of source code; proprietary software restricts it under license

name: System Software vs Application Software (concept)
expr: system software manages hardware and runs the computer (e.g. OS); application software performs user tasks

name: Compiler Error vs Runtime Error (concept)
expr: a compiler error is caught before the program runs; a runtime error occurs while the program is executing

name: Digital Divide (concept)
expr: the gap between those who have easy access to computers/internet and those who do not

name: Data vs Information (concept)
expr: data is raw, unprocessed facts; information is data that has been processed into a meaningful form

name: BFS Complexity
expr: O(V + E), V = vertices, E = edges

name: DFS Complexity
expr: O(V + E), V = vertices, E = edges

name: Dijkstra's Algorithm Complexity
expr: O((V + E) log V) using a priority queue (min-heap)

name: Bellman-Ford Algorithm Complexity
expr: O(V × E), handles negative edge weights

name: Floyd-Warshall Algorithm Complexity
expr: O(V³), finds shortest paths between all pairs

name: Kruskal's Algorithm Complexity
expr: O(E log E), builds Minimum Spanning Tree by sorting edges

name: Prim's Algorithm Complexity
expr: O(E log V), builds Minimum Spanning Tree using a priority queue

name: Topological Sort Complexity
expr: O(V + E), valid only for a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)

name: Edges in a Complete Graph
expr: E = n(n − 1)/2, for n vertices

name: AVL Tree Balance Factor
expr: BF = Height(Left Subtree) − Height(Right Subtree), must be −1, 0, or 1

name: Height of a Balanced Binary Tree
expr: h = O(log n), for n nodes

name: B-Tree Order (Max Children/Keys)
expr: Max children = m, Max keys per node = m − 1, for order m

name: Red-Black Tree Property (concept)
expr: a self-balancing BST where every node is red or black and root-to-leaf paths have the same number of black nodes

name: Trie (concept)
expr: a tree-like structure that stores strings by sharing common prefixes among nodes

name: Hash Function (concept)
expr: a function that maps input data of arbitrary size to a fixed-size value (hash code)

name: Load Factor (Hash Table)
expr: Load Factor = n/m, n = number of entries, m = number of buckets

name: Hash Table Search Complexity
expr: Average = O(1), Worst = O(n), worst case occurs with many collisions

name: 0/1 Knapsack Recurrence
expr: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i−1][w], dp[i−1][w−wt[i]] + val[i])

name: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) Recurrence
expr: if match: dp[i][j] = dp[i−1][j−1] + 1, else: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i−1][j], dp[i][j−1])

name: Fibonacci via Dynamic Programming
expr: DP complexity = O(n), versus naive recursive complexity = O(2ⁿ)

name: Memoization vs Tabulation (concept)
expr: memoization is top-down recursion with caching; tabulation is bottom-up iterative table filling

name: Greedy Algorithm (concept)
expr: builds a solution step by step, always choosing the locally optimal option at each step

name: Optimal Substructure (concept)
expr: a problem has optimal substructure if an optimal solution can be built from optimal solutions of its subproblems

name: Phases of a Compiler (concept)
expr: Lexical Analysis → Syntax Analysis → Semantic Analysis → Intermediate Code → Optimization → Code Generation

name: Lexical Analysis (concept)
expr: converts source code into a stream of tokens by removing whitespace and comments

name: Parsing — LL vs LR (concept)
expr: LL parsers scan input left-to-right building a leftmost derivation; LR parsers build a rightmost derivation in reverse

name: Symbol Table (concept)
expr: a data structure storing information about identifiers such as variables, functions, and their attributes

name: Three Address Code (concept)
expr: an intermediate representation where each instruction has at most three operands, e.g. t1 = t2 + t3

name: Context-Free Grammar (CFG)
expr: G = (V, T, P, S), V = variables, T = terminals, P = production rules, S = start symbol

name: COCOMO Basic Model — Effort
expr: Effort = a × (KLOC)^b person-months

name: COCOMO Basic Model — Development Time
expr: Time = c × (Effort)^d months

name: Function Point (FP) (concept)
expr: a measure of software size based on the functionality delivered to the user, independent of technology

name: Cyclomatic Complexity
expr: V(G) = E − N + 2, E = edges, N = nodes in control flow graph

name: Defect Density
expr: Defect Density = Number of Defects/Size (KLOC)

name: Shannon Entropy
expr: H(X) = −Σ p(x) log₂ p(x)

name: Information Content
expr: I(x) = −log₂ p(x)

name: Huffman Coding (concept)
expr: builds a variable-length prefix code assigning shorter codes to more frequent symbols to minimize average length

name: Compression Ratio
expr: Compression Ratio = Uncompressed Size/Compressed Size

name: RSA Key Generation (concept)
expr: choose primes p, q; n = p×q; compute φ(n) = (p−1)(q−1); pick e coprime to φ(n); find d = e⁻¹ mod φ(n)

name: RSA Encryption
expr: C = M^e mod n

name: RSA Decryption
expr: M = C^d mod n

name: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange (concept)
expr: allows two parties to jointly establish a shared secret key over an insecure channel without transmitting it directly

name: Digital Signature (concept)
expr: a sender encrypts a message hash with their private key so a receiver can verify authenticity using the public key

name: Support (Association Rule)
expr: Support(A→B) = P(A ∩ B)

name: Confidence (Association Rule)
expr: Confidence(A→B) = P(B | A)

name: Lift (Association Rule)
expr: Lift(A→B) = Confidence(A→B)/Support(B)

name: CAP Theorem (concept)
expr: a distributed system can guarantee at most two of: Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance

name: MapReduce (concept)
expr: a programming model that processes large datasets by splitting work into parallel Map and Reduce tasks

name: Block Hash (concept)
expr: a unique fixed-size digital fingerprint of a block's data, including the previous block's hash, linking the chain

name: Merkle Tree (concept)
expr: a binary tree of hashes where each leaf is a data hash and each parent is the hash of its children, used to verify data integrity

name: Proof of Work (concept)
expr: a consensus mechanism requiring miners to solve a computationally difficult puzzle to validate and add a new block

name: Convolution Operation (concept)
expr: slides a filter/kernel over an input to produce a feature map by computing element-wise products and summing

name: TF-IDF (Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency)
expr: TF-IDF = TF × log(N/DF), N = total documents, DF = documents containing the term

name: N-gram (concept)
expr: a contiguous sequence of n items (words or characters) from a given text, used in language modeling
